messages.text: Still on for Thursday coffee? I can bring that ladder if you are doing gutter work again.
Yes, 10 works. Elena says the gutter part can wait until after the $386 lens repair clears.
Good call. One surprise at a time.
We moved it from checking this morning, so no drama. I just do not want to crowd the house payment that posts Friday.
The dental statement posted this morning. Can you take the chicken out of the freezer before your walk?
Marisol said she can leave Shoreline after her morning staff huddle, but only if the 2:00 patient-scheduling meeting ends on time.
Yes. I will make rice and calabacitas tonight instead of stopping by the place near the ferry.
Good. I will start the beans late so they are warm when they get here.
Good. I also moved the Leavenworth folder off this month's calendar until we see the lens repair amount.
Please pull the small folding mattresses from the hall closet. Just one night, then she picks them up before lunch Sunday.
I will set out the blue towels and keep the driveway clear for her car.
That is fine. I would rather use the vegetables before they go soft anyway.
The county guide is still on the table. I put sticky notes by schools, clinic funding, and the shoreline rule.
Good. I also marked the judge race where one candidate keeps saying the last count was stolen.
You crossed out the one with the big promises on every page?
Yes. I want steady people who will protect the schools and clinics, not just make noise.
Dad, are you and Mom putting the Peoria stream on tonight or saving your eyes for tomorrow?
We have it on low while Elena folds laundry. She already asked if your brother-in-law is still coming Sunday for the blue-and-green replay.
Dad, could you look at my after-school song worksheet? Half the kids read faster in Spanish, half in English, and I want it to land for both.
Dad, for the Edmonds place, do you want quiet guitar under the opening night or just the objects doing the talking?
Send it. Keep the directions short and put the vocabulary in two columns before the activity.
Maybe just a few songs at the start. I want people to stop at each shelf and read the little family cards.
Tell her yes. I may call in for the fourth quarter if rehearsal ends early.
That sounds like your old binder system.
Makes sense. If kids bring drawings too, I can help you arrange them so they don't look like an afterthought.
Good. I will keep the snacks simple so everyone can actually see the screen.
Some of those habits came from my methods courses, some from room 214 when the copy machine was always broken.
Good. The young ones should be next to the old photos, not separated.
Hermano, you sounded quiet yesterday. Did you and Elena get outside after breakfast?
Yes, we walked by the ferry landing. Then I sanded the small frame for Marisol's photo.
Good. Mama always said your hands needed work when your head was too full.
Elena made coffee and sat with me before bills. That helped too.
Vi la foto vieja de Elena contigo, la del baile antes de que te quedaras en Washington. Todavia la guardo.
Te mande las fotos de la fiesta de San Jose por la pagina azul. Avisame si las viste.
Mandamela cuando puedas. A Elena le va a dar risa verla despues del desayuno aqui en Edmonds.
Las vi esta manana. Entre un momento, guarde dos fotos y sali antes de leer todos los comentarios.
Carlos, encontre unas fotos viejas: tu con carteles de alebrijes y los muchachos poniendo papel picado en el pasillo.
Encontré la foto vieja de la casa por el Llano. Salen Mamá, Papá, tú con uniforme, yo chiquita y los demás en la puerta.
Esa sirve para la página de recuerdos. ¿Se alcanza a ver la calle o solo el patio?
Guardalas por favor. Ese ano tambien hice la version en espanol de los folletos para las familias.
Mejor asi. Una prima puso una cosa rara sobre las vacunas.
Claro. Dile que se ve igual de seria y bonita. ?Siguen usando la mesa chica junto a la ventana?
Si no trae fuente clara, lo dejo pasar. Luego te llamo y hablamos tranquilos.
Se ve el patio y el cuarto donde se quedaba Abuela algunas temporadas. También tengo una hoja de Santo Domingo con tu nombre escrito a mano.
Y en la caja hay recibos con descuentos pequenos de cada mes, todos engrapados al talon de pago.
Si, esa misma. Dos platos casi todas las mananas, y las sillas extras esperando visitas.
Guárdala, por favor. Quiero comparar esos datos con lo que tengo aquí antes de escribirlo.
Esos papeles servian cuando revisabamos el horario, los pasos de sueldo y las horas de preparacion.
Vi la foto del cuaderno con la taza azul. Esa lluvia en la ventana parece de nuestra casa vieja.
Anoche agregue dos paginas despues de leer un poco de Neruda. La taza azul queda en la mesa para no olvidar a Mama.
Pon tambien cuando Papa limpiaba los zapatos antes de ir al aula. Eso dice mucho sin hacerlo grande.
Si. Ese detalle va bajo el titulo Clay, Chalk, and Rain, junto con el patio despues del aguacero.
Dad, can you send me the photo of abuelo with the old guitar? The kids at the Rosewood room are making a wall timeline for Saturday.
I have it in the blue envelope. Is this for the group near 82nd again?
Yes. Same Portland crew, but this week they asked how songs travel with families and why some neighborhoods lose after-school space first.
I will scan it after dinner. Your mother says to remind me if it needs to be clear enough for a projector.
Carlos, Elena told me you were looking at old photos again. The ones with the red temple gates?
Encontré otra caja en la casa: los cuadernos de mamá con sus cuentas de hilos y una libreta de papá con dibujos de jarritos.
Si, and also a map of northern Spain. Just looking after breakfast, nothing serious.
Guárdalos, por favor. Esas cuentas y dibujos dicen más que muchas fotografías.
Carlos, encontre otra foto de mama con las velas de la mesa grande. Te la mando por WhatsApp.
Gracias, Tere. Elena quiere poner esa foto con la de papa este ano. Se va a ver bonita.
Looking is free. But promise me you two choose places where you can rest in the afternoons.
También hay dos certificados viejitos, los dos dicen sexto. Están manchados de humo y polvo rojo.
That is the whole idea. Trains, short walks, and Elena saying no to my stubbornness.
Eso suena a la casa completa: mesa de hilos de un lado, barro secándose del otro.
Tambien guarde semilla de cempasuchil del patio. Si alguien viaja al norte, te mando un sobre.
Que bien. Aqui no siempre sale igual, pero me gusta intentar con algo de alla.
La foto del pozole se ve buenisima. Ese verde encima se parece al de nuestra casa vieja.
Corte un poco de cilantro de las macetas de atras y Elena dijo que no pusiera tanto chile.
Jaja, ella sabe. Tambien vi algo amarillo detras de la olla en la foto.
Son los primeros calendulas que abrieron junto a la cerca.
Ese plato rojo que mandaste se veía muy rico. ¿Era el caldo con oregano de tu jardin?
Si, lo puse junto a la ventana para que saliera el vapor. Luego lo subi con una nota corta del oregano.
Me dio hambre verlo. Manda otro cuando hagas el mole de Elena.
Voy a revisar primero en la laptop; la luz quedo un poco amarilla en el telefono.
Ya vi la foto del oregano, hermano. Aqui tambien esta pegando bonito el sol.
Que bueno. Elena dijo que el pozole salio mejor con el que corte ayer.
Manda una nota de voz manana si puedes; se corto poquito cuando hablaste desde la cocina.
Si, manana te mando audio despues de caminar.
I found the $25 card charge from last night. Was that the table by the fountain?
Yes, the young woman with the clipboard. Small amount, but it seemed useful.
Also the mail ballots came. We can read the voter guide after lunch, before your 2:30 clinic message comes in.
Good. I want to compare the school levy notes with the library page, and I will follow what Dr. Han sends.
Vi tu foto del caldo. Le pusiste oregano del patio?
Si, y guajillo. Hoy dejo listo el maiz para que Elena no tenga que estar parada en la cocina.
Asi lo hacia Mama, con calma desde temprano.
Me falta pasar por rabanos y limones despues de caminar.
That library board clip I sent is already full of chanting from both sides. Coffee Thursday may be easier than watching all of it.
I saw two minutes and closed it. I would rather hear your version over coffee and take the long way past the marina.
Fair. Bring the mystery novel if you finished the chapter.
That is the plan tonight: book after supper, not the panel people talking over each other.
Before you stop at QFC, please look at the March sheet. We have $1,384 marked after the power bill and pharmacy.
I saw it. I only added coffee, oranges, and the fish for tonight.
Good. Keep the receipt in the blue folder, not your jacket pocket.
Yes, jefa. I will bring it home flat this time.
Do you still want the son jarocho tracks for the kids' art morning?
Yes, send two if they are calm enough for cutting paper. I already spent about 2 hours on the photo cards.
I'll email them tonight. Funny how your old lesson-planning brain still shows up.
It keeps my hands busy without a bell schedule. Saturday is 10 to 1, then I am done.
Pavement looks dry now. I left the lighter jacket by the back door.
Gracias. I'll take the small binoculars and be back before the laundry finishes.
Please use the flatter side near the marsh today. Your knee was talking last night.
Yes, easy route today. If the clouds lower, I'll turn around early.
I left your blue cap by the door. The tide chart says the beach steps may be wet.
Gracias. I saw three notes from the marsh already, so I will go slow and stay on the dry side.
Take the phone in case your knee complains. Coffee after?
Yes. I only want the salt air a while and maybe the bench where the gulls pass low.
I put the blue envelopes next to your glasses. The county booklet is open to the school district page.
Gracias. I want to reread that one after the PBS segment from last night.
Also check the library page. You underlined two notes there but did not choose anything yet.
Leave it out for lunch. I still have the Herald article folded inside.
Dad, when you go through the March envelopes, do not toss the pharmacy receipts. Elena asked me which card paid first.
I put them in the blue folder with the clinic paper. The refill was only $11 after they ran both cards.
Good. Also, that brochure with the daily-helper rates is separate from regular visits. Bring it Sunday and I can look at the fine print.
Gracias, mija. Those numbers feel heavier than the office bills.
Coffee Thursday still good? I can choose the place with fewer stairs this time.
Yes. Elena has the stair-rail fellow coming that morning, so 10:45 works better.
Good. Stay out of the crawl space yourself. People from the class of '48 don't need to be wrestling with insulation.
I only point and make coffee now. No extra hands living here to blame if I overdo it.
Marisol left the voter guide by your chair. The city page has that question you marked about who answers certain 911 calls.
Gracias. I want to compare the answers with the chart from Wednesday, especially the stops near schools.
Also Mrs. Rojas asked if you still have the yellow copy from that morning on 84th. She sounded nervous about the wording.
I kept it in the blue folder. I can explain the form again after Mass, just the plain words.
For my visit, want to do Carkeek or keep it closer to the water?
Closer to the water sounds better. The class Tuesday already gave me enough floor work for the week.
Waterfront it is. I'll bring coffee and we can take the benches route.
Perfect. Benches route lets me keep a steady pace.
Do you still have the little school-garden piece from last month? The youth group wants examples of quiet places.
Yes, it is drying in the small back room. I can take a clean picture after I clear the boxes from the table.
No rush. If you find the old courtyard photos too, those might help with the workshop memory prompt.
I put those in a folder named Oaxaca-courtyard, but I need to crop a few crooked edges.
Encontré una foto tuya con la chamarra café. Mamá escribió atrás: verano 72, ya lejos de Oaxaca.
Guárdala, por favor. Esa chamarra salió conmigo y todavía me acompañó en California.
También hay una carta donde dices que Elena te esperaba al norte, cerca de las escuelas.
Sí, esa carta fue de los años en que todo se acomodó, aunque yo no lo sabía todavía.
Hermano, tengo tos desde ayer. Mi comadre dice un te de hojas fuertes, pero no se.
Hazte tu caldito y manzanilla, descansa, y llama a la clinica si sigue. No mezcles cosas raras sin preguntar.
Si, voy a rezar tambien. Tu brazo como va despues de lo de la farmacia?
Un poco pesado nada mas. El papel del farmaceutico decia hielo y agua; Elena ya puso sopa.
Antes de que salgas, Teresa dejo dos mensajes anoche. Dice que la fiesta en el barrio empieza el domingo.
Los vi. Le contestare despues del cafe con Bill, con calma.
Tambien pregunta si todavia tienes aquellas hojas viejas de lectura, las de una pagina para cada idioma.
Creo que estan en la caja del garage, con los planes de clase.
Dad, if the retired teachers do that lunch again, are you going?
Maybe after the first rush. I do better when it is just Bill, Elena, and one more chair.
That sounds more like you. Did you ever finish the little wash you started after Martin's service?
Almost. I added the green mug on the table. Bill will notice it tomorrow.
Coffee still 10? Weather says the marina path should stay dry.
10 works. I did my slow mat hour Tuesday, so today I would rather keep the walk level.
Good. No bluff trail then. I have a school board article to show you.
Still on for 10? I have the school board clipping and exactly one bad joke about lab goggles.
I put the school board article where the retired teachers can see it. One reply is already turning sideways.
Coffee still 10? I saved the KUOW piece on the board candidates, if you want the link.
Yes. Same table if it is open. I am bringing the small painting; no speech, just want your eye on it.
I saw your post after breakfast. Good article. I will read the link, but I am staying out of the replies.
Yes, send it. I was comparing that race with the county booklet and got stuck on two answers.
Good. Two cups and no committee meeting. My kind of morning.
I'll bring the Tribune clipping too. The levy wording is a mess, even for retired teachers.
Wise. Coffee still 10?
Yes. Tell me the science version at the table, not under that post.
Coffee at 10 still? I saved you the Herald piece on the school board race.
Good. I do not want to guess on that one.
Still 10. I want to read the part about the classroom list and the candidate refusing the certification question.
The science curriculum paragraph made me sigh into my oatmeal.
Bring it. I also have the note on the wage ordinance and the clinic van proposal.
Coffee still at 10? I can meet near Walnut if you want the flatter route.
Let's do Walnut, then maybe the marina rail. Someone marked scoters there at 8:05.
Still on for coffee at 10? Rain is backing off.
I'll bring the little field guide. Wind looks mild for once.
Yes. I did the usual breakfast, stretched the knee, and let two guitar pieces play before leaving.
Good. A few minutes watching the water before coffee will make the school-board talk easier.
Good sequence. Bring the small carving if it fits in your coat pocket.
Still on for 10? I can grab the corner table.
I will. No appointments to rush to after, just home for lunch with Elena.
Almost there. I came through Pine Ridge first and had to wipe mud off my shoes.
Bring the glasses in with you. I want to see if those were the same little brown ones by my feeder.
They're in my bag. Slow miles first, coffee second.
Did the Edmonds thing stay calm? Portland friends were asking about the signs.
For the youth workshop, can I say the tin animals came from the same streets as your first family papers?
Dad, did you try that Son Jarocho record with the new speakers?
Very calm. A few teachers, church people, students. I stood near the edge and listened more than shouted.
Say they connect to our family papers and the old house, not more than that. I want the story careful.
Putting it on now. I left the remote in the drawer before the guests on TV started doing their finger-pointing.
Good trade. I can send the youth ensemble playlist too.
Send it. I also opened the photo folder from your last visit, so the night will be music and pictures.
That sounds like you. For my youth workshop, do you still like using the public library room?
Got it. Also, was the cousin in that house during your school-uniform photo, or later?
Yes. Libraries and schools are where young people can actually walk in. Just keep the city complaint-board clipping out of the kid handouts.
Around that period. Not always there, but enough that I remember another place at the table.
Dad, for my youth arts budget, do you still have an old narrative that got classroom money approved?
I can scan one. It had goals, family night, materials, and a small evaluation page.
Perfect. Also, do those old step charts explain why your June pay changed after year 10?
Yes. Look for the chart with columns, not the handwritten notes from the principal.
Coffee still good at 10? Weather says showers by noon.
Yes. I need to rinse mud off first. I was tying up the little pepper plants and trimming the purple salvia.
Bring one of those tiny peppers if they survived. My soup needs a warning label.
They are still small, but I can bring dried ones from last year.
Javier called while you were outside. He can come up from Portland on the 27th if his Thursday lessons do not move.
Good. I will leave the guest room books in the closet and not on the bed.
He also asked if you saved the voter-guide page about school funding. He said his teenagers are comparing it with their bus-pass problem.
I saved it. We can talk after lunch before I forget where I put it.
Dad, one of my youth arts kids asked why adults talk different when a badge is nearby. Hard question for a trumpet warmup.
They notice more than people think. Sometimes the same sentence lands different from an old man with my accent.
That is exactly what I was trying to say without making the room heavy.
Tell them calm voices help, and records help too. Memory alone is too easy for the powerful to brush aside.
Dad, Tia Lupita sent a Facebook post about the new spring COVID appointment. Please don't forward that one.
I won't. I looked at the state page this morning and saved Dr. Chen's portal note.
Good. Bartell can print the timing sheet too if you ask at pickup.
I will ask. Elena is making arroz caldo tonight, so we keep it simple after errands.
I am still in Shoreline. The benefits-enrollment batch crashed right before I was leaving.
No hurry. Elena kept the soup low and I saved two small bowls.
Can we do just dinner tonight? They have soccer at 9 tomorrow and I did not pack pajamas.
Dinner only is fine. I will put the booster cushion back in the closet after.
Hermano, did the second deposit arrive today like you expected?
Yes, the $3,075 is there. Elena already put a little note beside it before I finished lunch.
She has always been careful with the papers. Tell her I send a hug.
I will. She also circled what we can send after the dentist check clears.
Carlos, Elena me dijo que guardas una libretita con tus numeros de la manana. Todo bien esta semana?
Si, hermana. La pastilla chica ya esta en la caja de domingo a sabado, y anote 128/76 esta manana.
Que bueno. Aca una vecina paga mucho por alguien que la ayuda cada dia en casa. Da miedo pensar en esos gastos.
Eso mismo me preocupa mas que las citas normales. Por ahora el deposito mensual y lo guardado nos alcanzan.
For Thursday coffee, bring that old faculty badge if you still have it. The retired teachers table will get a kick out of the hair.
That heron frame from the marina looked sharper than your usual phone ones. New lens behaving?
I found it with a 1975 classroom list and an envelope from California. The hair is worse than you remember.
The repair helped. I carried the small camera this morning, then cleaned the edge on the laptop before putting it up.
Was that the year you stopped circling back and just kept the classroom keys?
I noticed it between a watercolor page and a museum sketch in my feed. Quite the neighborhood you keep there.
Close enough. By then the kids needed someone who understood the hallway silence.
Those accounts teach my eye. The bird was just patient with me today.
For my April visit, should I bring the folding cot or is the back room cleared?
Back room is yours. It only has Elena's sewing boxes and my camera tripod right now.
Good. I worried someone might be using it after the shower work started.
No, just your mother and me. The grab bars are so we keep the morning routine simple.
Do you want us there before the 1:05 start or just after lunch?
Before is better. Your mother is making rice and I moved the small table so the children can sit near the couch.
Okay. Mateo also wants to know if abuelo still has the Wilson jersey in the closet.
Yes, but he has to wash his hands before touching it. I still remember the nacho cheese from last time.
Dad, I can help compare the dental estimate if Mom wants another set of eyes.
Gracias. It came to $412 if they do the extra x-ray. Elena already marked the amount in the checkbook.
Okay. Any other monthly payments I should factor if we sort the timing?
Just the house one and normal bills. The card is paid when the statement arrives.
Mom asked me how to track fare alerts without getting twenty emails a day.
She is organized. I only saved two: Bilbao in September and Osaka in late October.
Please add extra connection time. No heroic airport sprinting.
Already told her: if the numbers or the walking look foolish, we close the laptop.
We can bring drinks tomorrow. Do you need anything for the kids?
Bring containers if you want leftovers. I already have the hominy, pork shoulder, and cabbage.
Perfect. Mom said she is staying out of your way until the pot is done.
Good plan. She can tell me if I forgot the napkins.
We can still bring the kids Sunday. Do you want us to pick up teriyaki on the way?
No, mija. I have beans soaking and Elena bought chicken thighs. We will eat here.
Okay. Mom said you two moved that overnight coast idea. Everything alright?
All right. Just giving March a little room before we choose new dates.
Mom said you found the box with the 1978 church photo. Can I scan it next time I'm in Edmonds?
Yes. Elena put it near the hallway closet so we won't forget.
I'll come Sunday after lunch. Need me to bring anything for the house?
Just yourself. We have enough for our usual two plates, and I can add more rice when you arrive.
Encontraste la foto de mamá junto al puesto de flores?
Sí. La puse con las otras de Oaxaca, y también hice una versión menos amarilla para que se vea su vestido.
Mándamela cuando puedas. Y guarda bien las figuritas, no quiero que se rompan.
Están arriba del librero en el cuarto pequeño, lejos de las bandejas y los papeles húmedos.
Te mande la foto de mama con la olla grande. Se ve un poco borrosa, pero la cara de ella esta clara.
Gracias. I can place it near the small cup, with the story about her lending it for baptisms.
Ponlo tambien en ingles para tus nietos. Ellos deben saber por que esa olla viajaba de casa en casa.
Yes, one side for them and one side for us. I will keep it short enough for the card.
Thursday coffee still good? I can bring the old bilingual primer I found in the garage.
Yes, please bring it. I am trying to get the classroom chapter right, especially the small things on the desk.
You also wanted that slim Epictetus copy back. I marked the page with the cup stain.
That page helped last night. It slowed me down enough to write about Papa's hands instead of making a speech.
For the youth workshop, should I bring rhythm tracks or let your photos carry it?
Bring soft tracks. I have one photo of my mother measuring blue thread and one of my father polishing a black bowl.
That pairing will work. Do you want me to print captions in Spanish and English?
Yes, but keep them simple. Mention they both left books early and learned mostly with their hands.
Dad, I found the orange paper flowers from last year in my garage. Want me to bring them Sunday?
Yes, please. Your mother saved the little clay dishes too, so we will not need to buy many things.
I'll also bring the photo of abuelo that Javier scanned. The kids asked why we always leave the good bread out.
I can explain it at dinner, slowly. Some things are easier when they see us do them.
For Thursday coffee, bring that old packet you mentioned. The new board member keeps asking what kids actually needed before they could write a full paragraph.
I can bring the one with picture cards, sentence frames, and the family letter in Spanish on the back.
Perfect. Also, did your campus keep copies of those field journals? Mine disappeared in a basement leak.
I found two journals in the UW box. Lots of notes on small groups and how to stop translating every line.
I put your center folder by the coffee. Are you taking the 11:30 bus or should I drop you after the pharmacy?
Bus is fine. Today is only planning, noon to 2. I need to leave space for my knee.
Good. Last week you came home tired after the Saturday table.
I know. This week should be around six hours total, including the phone check-ins with the two boys.
I found the envelope with Martin's photo by your brushes. Do you want it on the table tonight?
Yes, beside the blue cup. Tomorrow I may ask Bill if he remembers the ferry story.
Good. Keep tomorrow simple, Carlos. Coffee and one story at a time.
That is enough. After dinner I will finish the sky wash.
Coffee at 10 still? I brought the article about the school board dustup and the library budget.
Still on. I also clipped the Herald note about the review panel. The language was careful, but the numbers deserved a harder look.
You and your margins. Did Elena say anything about your evening downtown adventure?
She said my knees complained more than I did. I put in a little money and came home before dark.
Dad, I sent the playlist from my students' recital. Track 3 has the nylon-string piece you liked.
I put it on after dinner while Elena read. It settled the house nicely.
Did you still paint the little shelf today?
One coat only. Walk first, brush after, no hurrying.
Before I recycle the duplicate folders, do you want the notes from the two new classroom people you helped that spring?
Keep one set. The sample lesson and parent letter might help Javier.
I also found the building-rep card and the packet with Article 9 marked in yellow.
Save those with the pay charts. They explain why lunch duty and planning minutes mattered.
I put Teresa's envelope on your desk. The thin paper with the parish stamp is fragile, so don't feed it through the scanner.
I'll photograph it by the window. The names line up with Mamá and Papá exactly as I remembered.
There is also a note on the back of the patio photo: you, Teresa, two brothers, Abuela, and that cousin with the serious face.
That must be from the school years before I left. Please keep it with the Oaxaca folder.
Dad, I can print the city packet before Sunday dinner. Do you want the page with injury numbers or the call-diversion budget page?
Both, please. Numbers should not disappear into a paragraph.
I also found a Spanish version of the traffic court explainer, but it is written like a machine did it.
Send it. If Mrs. Rojas brings her copy Sunday, I can mark the confusing parts.
Dad, did you see the hospital association scorecard? The candidate you liked answered the interpreter question clearly.
I saw. Also liked her answer on keeping the neighborhood clinic open on Saturdays.
The other one dodged everything and then went back to talking about suspicious ballots.
That is why I moved him to the bottom of my notes.
Tia Lupe tagged you in that clinic-share thing. Please don't answer her there.
I only opened it because she used my name. I asked her to send the clinic website, then closed it.
Good. I can check the website after dinner.
Gracias. I would rather ask you than spend the evening under someone else's post.
Thursday coffee still on? I can meet at the usual cafe or walk by the marina if you are avoiding the pastries.
Coffee is fine. I packed oatmeal before leaving, so just one cup for me.
Sensible. Did you ever book that train over the mountains?
Not yet. Elena and I are waiting a bit after the repair shop called.
I opened the county notice. Property tax first half is due April 30, same amount as last year.
Okay. I will put it with the credit union envelope and the insurance renewal.
Also, the clinic refunded $37 to checking. I put it against groceries.
Good. After the Friday transfer we still have enough set aside for anything small that comes up.
Before the kids arrive, can you move your laptop from the kitchen table? The plate with the blue napkin is still on the screen.
I am almost done. I only wanted to straighten it before I share it.
Use the darker bowl next time. The salsa looked better in that one.
Good eye. I saved that idea next to the museum tile page I was looking at.
Did Marisol make it up from Shoreline with the little crew, or did her clinic paperwork win again?
They came yesterday after six. The house was loud in a good way.
Tell them I owe them a drum lesson next time. Are they using my old room tonight?
No, Marisol is taking them back after lunch. Elena already washed the guest sheets from last time.
I can drive up from Portland the 28th. Is the guest room free or did Marisol claim it?
Free. Elena changed the sheets after the kids left, and it has been quiet since.
Good. I'll bring the guitar and stay one night.
That works. I will clear the extra chair in the kitchen; most days it just holds mail.
I found the folder from your old classroom box. There are interview pages from the elder project and a few color-pencil market scenes.
Those would help. The center asked for things that show more than objects on shelves.
I'll bring the folder Sunday. Want me to separate the Spanish drafts from the English final copies?
Please. Some pairs should stay together so people can see how the children moved between both.
Dad, Javier texted me the flyer draft from Portland. Can you check the Spanish line before he prints it?
Send it here. Is it for the room with the drums and the mural wall?
